messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient Name: Not Specified
Gender: Male
Age: 50
Date of Admission: Not Specified
Date of Discharge: Not Specified
Date of Dictation: Not Specified

HOSPITAL COURSE:

The patient is a 50-year-old male who presented with hoarseness and shortness of breath. The patient was diagnosed with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL), stage IV, after Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy revealed intratracheal mass in right main bronchi with complete right mainstem bronchus occlusion. The patient underwent several treatment regimens, including Dose Adjusted R-EPOCH therapy, R2-CHOP-I therapy, PD-1 inhibitor, DNMTi and the combination of decitabine, sintilimab plus HDACi (Chidamide). The patient experienced myelosuppression and achieved partial remission.

The patient was treated using venetoclax in combination with Chidamide, Sintilimab and radiotherapy after the PD was seen in repeat PET-CT. The patient experienced a decrease in lesion size and FDG uptake. The patient later underwent syngeneic stem cell transplantation and achieved CR.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:

1. It is important to continue the follow-up care with your oncologist.
2. Please continue to take medications as prescribed and follow the recommended dosing schedule.
3. Follow the recommended diet and nutrition plan given by your oncologist.
4. It is important to stay hydrated to the recommended level of fluid intake.
5. Follow the recommended activity guidelines set by your oncologist.
6. Please report any side effects or unusual symptoms to your oncologist immediately.
7. Follow the recommendations for required tests and imaging studies.
8. Follow recommendations for self-care and regular follow-up appointments.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, stage IV, is the condition chiefly responsible for this admission; the hoarseness and breathlessness were presenting symptoms of the bronchial mass. It is a malignant neoplasm, chapter C. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma falls under category C83 (non-follicular lymphoma, C83.3).

CODE: C83
